system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Buyer review — Project Kestrel

The Seller’s update is **not an agreed position**. Recommendations below are buyer-side negotiating proposals, based on the supplied extracts; the underlying DD documents and complete SPA still require review.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | Meaningful general warranty recovery, with separate protection for higher-risk categories. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, subject to diligence and recovery security; exclude separately negotiated categories from this cap. **Reason:** A 20% cap leaves substantial acquisition risk with the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket and aggregation of related claims. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, with related claims aggregated and category-specific exclusions. **Reason:** The proposed combination can eliminate recovery for numerous meaningful losses. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | General warranties: **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least two reporting cycles to identify general breaches, without shortening other claim periods. | **Seek 24 months**, with timely notified claims preserved and any proceedings deadline separately negotiated. **Reason:** Eighteen months may expire before latent issues emerge through financial reporting. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties share the general cap and time limit. | Separate, robust protection for authority, ownership, share capital and absence of encumbrances. | **Seek a separate 100%-of-price cap and seven-year notification period**, without de minimis, basket, disclosure or knowledge qualifications. **Reason:** The Buyer must receive the ownership and authority for which it pays AUD 24m. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception is supplied. | Express preservation of fraud claims and remedies, with appropriate attribution to the Seller. | **Carve fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation/concealment out of caps, contractual time bars, releases, non-reliance and exclusive-remedy provisions.** **Reason:** Broad boilerplate must not purport to shield fraudulent conduct or constrain available remedies. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, accounts, registers and public records, plus specific disclosures. | Only fair, sufficiently detailed disclosures against identified warranties; no disclosure defence to specific indemnities unless expressly agreed. | **Reject blanket deemed disclosure; require specific cross-references, sufficient detail to understand nature and scope, and a frozen, retained disclosure bundle.** **Reason:** Document availability alone does not fairly explain a warranty exception or allocate its economic consequences. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer/advisers or discoverable from the data room/public records. | No constructive or imputed knowledge exclusion; preferably no knowledge defence at all. | **Delete clause 8.3; fallback only to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer individuals concerning the specific breach, with Seller bearing proof.** **Reason:** “Discoverable” information and adviser knowledge could defeat warranties despite inadequate disclosure. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure confirms no final consent or satisfaction evidence. | A binding consent satisfying clauses 11.2–11.3, effective at Completion, without unacceptable conditions or adverse contract changes. | **Keep a Buyer-waivable condition precedent requiring satisfactory consent and evidence all associated conditions are satisfied; include a long-stop termination right.** **Reason:** Written consent alone may not preserve a customer accounting for approximately 30% of FY26 revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Debt repaid and security/guarantees released at Completion under verified discharge arrangements. | **Require payout figures, direct repayment through funds flow and effective simultaneous discharge/release arrangements, with registry follow-through.** **Reason:** A debt-free/cash-free acquisition must not leave the target carrying Seller-era debt or security risk. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses are “for Seller” but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable employer on-costs, with clear payment and adjustment mechanics. | **Include verified amounts and applicable on-costs in funds flow or a specific price deduction, supported by an indemnity and no double counting.** **Reason:** Describing bonuses as Seller costs does not prevent the acquired company ultimately funding them. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; disclosure records **AUD 180,000 open**, but does not independently establish non-payment. | Verified ownership of all relevant deliverables and protection against losses arising from the identified payment/title defect. | **Verify payment status; require payment if outstanding and confirmatory assignment at/before Completion, plus a separate indemnity for resulting title, infringement, remediation and business-interruption losses.** **Reason:** Paying one invoice alone may neither establish complete IP ownership nor cover the consequences of defective title. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material; access, scope and notification requirements remain unresolved. | Prompt investigation, evidence preservation, lawful remediation/notification and allocation of pre-Completion incident costs. | **Require investigation updates and completion protections, plus a specific indemnity for resulting investigation, remediation and third-party/regulatory liabilities to the extent legally recoverable.** **Reason:** Uncertainty does not establish either a confirmed breach or absence of potentially material exposure. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals are ordinary-course costs. Disclosure leaves timing, scope, termination and accrual unresolved. | Assessment of all three commitments together, with correct treatment under interim covenants and price mechanics. | **Verify aggregate commitment, necessity, cancellation rights and accounting; seek Seller funding/price adjustment only where the agreed allocation warrants it.** **Reason:** Neither automatic ordinary-course treatment nor automatic debt classification is justified by the current evidence. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations and remedies apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and payment/completion obligations. | **Insert an express category matrix and precedence clause disapplying inappropriate caps, thresholds, time bars, disclosure and knowledge defences.** **Reason:** Otherwise broad “all Claims” wording can silently nullify separately negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register recording Seller ownership of 100%. | Independent confirmation of issued capital, legal/beneficial ownership, encumbrances and effective transfer mechanics. | **Reconcile the register with corporate records, certificates and issue/transfer history; investigate options, competing interests and security, and require executed transfer and registration deliverables.** **Reason:** The register is important evidence, not a substitute for title diligence and enforceable completion protections. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Treats tax and IP warranty positions as settled within the general regime. | Expressly negotiated tax and IP protections reflecting their distinct exposures. | **Keep both open: seek a pre-Completion tax indemnity and tailored tax warranties, generally seven-year protection; negotiate IP warranties, appropriate longer survival/cap and the separate Ironquay protection.** **Reason:** Neither category should become “settled” merely through the Seller’s assertion or default application of general limitations. |

**Immediate priorities:** Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, bonus funding and Ironquay ownership should be resolved through completion mechanics—not left solely to post-Completion warranty claims.
=== END ADVICE ===
